source.title: Grounding Large Language Models in Interactive Environments with Online Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Thomas Carta; Clément Romac; Thomas Wolf; Sylvain Lamprier; Olivier Sigaud; P. Oudeyer

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the scale-related downstream-performance version using task success after online RL fine-tuning, rather than held-out pretraining loss or power-law fitting.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling work and measures success rates for differently sized GFlan-T5 models after fine-tuning. This bears on V6, but it does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit loss-scaling laws, predict larger-run loss, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The size-ablation values are plotted rather than stated numerically.
record.test_reason: A small size ablation (Appendix B.5, Fig. 14) trains three GFlan-T5 sizes (80M, 780M, 3B) with online RL on one BabyAI-Text task. It bears only weakly on V6, as downstream success versus scale in a new setting. There is no loss, no fit and no prediction. Values are figure-only and averaged over 2 seeds. The paper's main results are about its GLAM grounding method, not scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that GLAM online RL grounding of Flan-T5 strongly improves sample efficiency and some zero-shot generalization over zero-shot Flan-T5, behavioural cloning and non-pretrained baselines. They add that model size strongly affects learning, which they liken to emergent abilities. They also note that compute costs limited them to small LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream task success after online RL fine-tuning across three model sizes; does not fit held-out-loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size changes the reported learning behavior in the Go to <object> task; the paper describes strong differences in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance between the 80 million and 780 million parameter models.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: For the size ablation, results are presented in a figure without numerical values in the text and are averaged over 2 seeds. The text does not describe the 3 billion parameter result separately. The evaluated outcome is task success after RL fine-tuning, not held-out pretraining loss or a fitted scaling law.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted. Other task-success and generalization results do not compare model size for V6; the paper's other size-related results do not measure a versioned claim.

untested.parts: Predictability: no fitted trend, no extrapolation, no link to pretraining loss; only 3 sizes, one task, after RL fine-tuning.
All; RL fine-tuning is studied, but no power-law form is examined.

record.verdict_notes: Marginal relevance to scaling laws. The size result is an appendix ablation of the authors' own RL method, cited to Kaplan and Wei et al., and is figure-only. A reader could reasonably treat this study as T6/discusses. Weight it very low in any V6 synthesis.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, and its dependence on compute.
Effect of architecture details such as depth and width at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

The study tests performance across model sizes only for its interactive BabyAI-Text setting after online RL fine-tuning; it does not test prediction from pretraining loss, a fitted scaling relationship, or downstream tasks beyond those reported.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: GFlan-T5 small
rows.stage_stated: online RL fine-tuning; trained for 400.000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Compared task success during online RL fine-tuning across GFlan-T5 model sizes.
rows.note: The authors state that prior knowledge appears impactful only when the network is large enough, and report a strong difference in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance between the 80 million and 780 million parameter models. No numeric value for this model is stated in the text.
rows.check: A single-model row is the comparison base, not an effect. It is only meaningful against r2. No value is stated; figure-only.

rows.subject: GFlan-T5 large
rows.stage_stated: online RL fine-tuning; trained for 400.000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Compared task success during online RL fine-tuning across GFlan-T5 model sizes.
rows.note: The authors report a strong difference in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance between this model and the 80 million parameter model; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Relative to r1 (80M), the text reports 'a strong difference on sample efficiency and asymptotic performance'. Improvement with size is stated qualitatively only, with no numbers.

rows.subject: GFlan-T5 XL
rows.stage_stated: online RL fine-tuning; trained for 400.000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Compared task success during online RL fine-tuning across GFlan-T5 model sizes.
rows.note: The figure includes this model, but the accompanying prose does not state its result separately or give its plotted values.
rows.check: The 3B result is plotted but never described in the text. Whether gains continue from 780M to 3B cannot be read.

relationships.condition: GFlan-T5 80M vs 780M (3B unreadable), Go To task, online PPO fine-tuning, 2 seeds
relationships.reason: Success improves strongly from 80M to 780M (r1, r2). The authors frame this as emergent, with prior knowledge impactful 'only when the network is large enough'. That is a threshold, not a smoothly predictable trend. The 3B result is unreported (r3), so the evidence is figure-only and thin.
relationships.display_finding: Success improved strongly from 80M to 780M across two seeds, which the authors interpreted as prior knowledge becoming useful only above a size threshold.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report a size-related difference in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance, but this is a narrow task setting and the results do not establish a predictable scaling relationship; see r1–r3.
